title: Tavi and the Mystery Tracks
markdown:
The sky burst open with brilliant pinks and dazzling golds. Sunlight poked the world awake. Tavi leaped out of bed. A fizz-pop excitement tickled her tummy.

“Pebble! Pebble, wake up!”

Pebble, a fluffy ball of white fur, thumped his tail. Thump-thump-thump! WOOF! WOOF! Today felt special. Crisp. Promising fun.

Outside, a thick blanket of fluffy snow glittered. Tavi tugged on bright red boots. CRUNCH! went each step. Pebble bounded ahead, kicking up powdery puffs. POW! Tiny clouds exploded with every paw-kick. They trotted down their favourite path, a clean white ribbon through the sleeping woods.

Tavi stopped. Bright eyes popped wide. “Pebble, look!”

Strange tracks dotted the snow. Not deer. Not fox. Peculiar. Some like tiny dots, packed tight. Others like little triangles with prongs. Some big, wonderfully splayed, like fluffy mittens. Pebble nudged a mitten-track with his wet nose. WOOF? Head tilt.

“Who made these weird tracks?” Tavi tapped her chin.

Mr Reed, their kind neighbour, ambled up, walking stick tapping a steady beat. “Good morning, Tavi! Pebble! What a puzzle you’ve found!” Happy thunder.

He peered close. “Nature plays clever tricks. Different creatures have special ways to get about.”

Tavi buzzed. “You mean the feet tell us who made the tracks?”

“Exactly. These tiny sharp prints — what has tiny sharp feet for gripping?” A flash of brilliant blue: a bold jay. Small feet barely disturbed the snow.

“A bird!” Tavi whispered.

“And these bigger ones. Spread out, like snowshoes. Why would an animal need big wide feet in deep snow?”

Tavi pictured Pebble’s paws — good for digging, but they’d sink. The mitten-tracks spread wide, like her own sturdy boots.

“So it doesn’t sink in! Like my boots!” She kicked a red boot. Pebble barked. WOOF!

They followed the tracks deeper, toward cozy pines. Branches tickled. In a warm hollow sat three plump snow hares, big furry hind feet tucked beneath them, white fur blending. Soft dark eyes. Peaceful.

Mr Reed smiled. “Special adaptations. Things that help them thrive. Wide furry feet. Built-in snowshoes. They hop right over the soft snow.”

Tavi beamed. Pebble’s bounce was perfect for fetch. The hares’ feet were perfect for snow. Her red boots were perfect for crunching. “Their feet are perfect for them.”

Reed agreed without a designed-just-so sermon. The hares blinked. The puzzle sat down in the snow and stayed, like a good boot print.

Tavi grinned. “Today is going to be AMAZING.” Pebble’s tail agreed. Thump-thump-thump. The woods, still sleeping, had already told on itself.
characters: Tavi (a young engineer), Pebble (a puppy), Reed (a neighbor)
author: StoryGen Community
